verdicts.missing_content: ClipSeg adds a FiLM-conditioned encoder-decoder on top of CLIP for zero-shot text/image-prompted segmentation. Useful but niche; SAM has overtaken it as the default promptable segmenter, and ClipSeg's mechanism (FiLM modulation of CLIP features) is a specialty that does not generalize to the LLM/VLM narrative. The book's coverage of CLIP (22.2) plus SAM (in 22.1 mention and 23.5 callout) already conveys the 'segment via foundation model' idea. A one-line ClipSeg name-drop in 22.3 could be added as historical context, but not a section.
verdicts.target_section: none (optional one-line mention in 22.x family rundown)

verdicts.missing_content: SAM (Meta, 2023) is the canonical promptable foundation segmenter: prompt encoders for point/box/mask/text (CLIP-projected), an MAE-pretrained heavy ViT image encoder, a lightweight transformer mask decoder with learnable mask tokens + IoU token, and the three-tier data engine (assisted-manual, semi-automatic, fully automatic) that bootstrapped the 1.1B-mask SA-1B dataset. FastSAM swaps the ViT for a YOLO/YOLACT prototype-coefficient pipeline and inverts the prompting (segment-everything-then-filter) with point containment, IoU filtering, and CLIP-text similarity post-processing. Ultralytics ships both behind a one-line API. The current book has only (a) a passing mention in 22.1's four-bucket taxonomy and (b) a 'Under the Hood: SAM' callout in 23.5 limited to 3D editing context. The core foundation-model-for-segmentation story, the SA-1B data-engine pattern (a teaching exemplar for foundation-model bootstrapping that mirrors LLM data curation), and the FastSAM speed/architecture tradeoff are absent. SAM is widely used in multimodal pipelines, document AI, computer-use agents, and grounded-VLM stacks (Grounded-SAM, SAM-2, LISA), so it deserves either a dedicated subsection in 22.x or a 'Vision Foundation Models beyond CLIP' sidebar in 22.2 or 22.3.
verdicts.target_section: new 22.3.x sidebar 'Vision Foundation Models beyond CLIP: SAM, SAM-2, FastSAM' OR a short subsection in 22.2 after SigLIP; cross-link from 23.5 and 29 (specialized agents)

verdicts.missing_content: Classification/detection/segmentation/face-analysis catalog with Ultralytics + HuggingFace recipes. Pure computer-vision survey content with no LLM/VLM dimension. The deck's only LLM-adjacent points (SAM, FastSAM, DETR-via-HF) are covered or addressed in the dedicated SAM/DETR verdicts above. No 'foundation-model-as-task-head' framing worth lifting into Ch 22 intro; the existing 22.1 four-bucket taxonomy (classifier/detector/segmenter/embedding) already does that job more crisply.

Capabilities tour of the Stable Diffusion ecosystem (text2img, img2img, inpainting, ControlNet pose/depth/Canny, multi-ControlNet, outpainting, LoRA, DreamBooth, Textual Inversion, ComfyUI, Civitai hub). Per the user's standing decision, Stable Diffusion is out of scope, and the deck contains nothing beyond SD. No spillover relevant to the LLM/VLM thread.

DETR pioneered the encoder-decoder transformer for set-prediction object detection: CNN backbone -> transformer encoder over the (H/32)x(W/32) feature map -> transformer decoder consuming 100 learned object queries that cross-attend to encoder outputs -> per-query (box, class) head, trained with Hungarian bipartite matching against ground-truth boxes (with a 'no object' class for unused slots). The mask head extension turns each query embedding into a per-instance mask via FPN-style multi-scale features, yielding panoptic segmentation. DETR is the textbook example of 'object queries as learnable detection slots' (a pattern reused in Mask2Former, OWL-ViT, and modern open-vocabulary detectors used by VLM pipelines and document AI). The book has zero mentions of DETR, object queries, or Hungarian matching. Since Ch 3 just gained encoder-decoder transformer coverage, a one-paragraph 'application: DETR' callout in Ch 3 or 22.1 would close the loop, illustrating how the encoder-decoder pattern transfers from translation to vision detection. Not a full section, but a high-value historical/conceptual bridge.
verdicts.target_section: short sidebar in Ch 3 (encoder-decoder applications) OR in 22.1 (vision-task taxonomy) noting DETR + object queries as the encoder-decoder transformer applied to detection

verdicts.missing_content: ImageGPT (Chen et al., 2020, OpenAI) applies the GPT-2 next-token recipe to images by k-means-quantizing pixels into a 512-value codebook, treating each pixel as a token (1024 tokens per 32x32 image), training a decoder-only transformer autoregressively to predict the next pixel, and then average-pooling token embeddings as a transferable image representation. This is the direct pre-VLM ancestor of (a) Parti and patch-token autoregressive image generators and (b) the discrete-token branch of any-to-any models like Chameleon (covered in 22.9) and Llama-4-Omni. The same logical slot as the just-added VisualBERT historical sidebar in 22.3: ImageGPT belongs as a one-paragraph 'pre-VLM lineage' sidebar showing that pixel-as-token autoregression preceded patch-token VLMs and underpins modern discrete-token omni models. Not a full section. Currently zero coverage.
verdicts.target_section: short historical sidebar in 22.3 (alongside VisualBERT sidebar) OR in 22.9 (omni models) as the autoregressive-pixel ancestor of Chameleon-style discrete-token any-to-any generation

top_false_negatives: SAM (1624): foundation promptable segmenter with SA-1B data-engine and FastSAM tradeoff; deserves a 22.x sidebar 'Vision Foundation Models beyond CLIP' with cross-links from Ch 23 and Ch 29 (specialized/computer-use agents).

DETR (2333): encoder-decoder transformer applied to object detection via learnable object queries + Hungarian matching; one-paragraph callout in Ch 3 or 22.1 bridges Ch 3's new encoder-decoder content to vision.
ImageGPT (2334): autoregressive pixel-token pre-VLM ancestor of Chameleon-style discrete-token any-to-any models; one-paragraph sidebar in 22.3 (next to VisualBERT) or in 22.9.
